# C standard datetime format codes mapping to regex patterns
_DT_FORMAT_CODES = {
    '%Y': r'\d{4}',      # Year with century
    '%y': r'\d{2}',      # Year without century (00-99)
    '%m': r'\d{1,2}',    # Month (01-12)
    '%d': r'\d{1,2}',    # Day (01-31)
    '%H': r'\d{1,2}',    # Hour (00-23)
    '%I': r'\d{1,2}',    # Hour (01-12)
    '%M': r'\d{1,2}',    # Minute (00-59)
    '%S': r'\d{1,2}',    # Second (00-59)
    '%f': r'\d{1,6}',    # Microseconds (000000-999999)
    '%z': r'[+-]\d{2}:?\d{2}',  # UTC offset +HHMM or +HH:MM
    '%Z': r'[A-Za-z_]+', # Timezone name
    '%a': r'[A-Za-z]+',  # Abbreviated weekday name
    '%A': r'[A-Za-z]+',  # Full weekday name
    '%b': r'[A-Za-z]+',  # Abbreviated month name
    '%B': r'[A-Za-z]+',  # Full month name
    '%c': r'.+',         # Locale's appropriate date and time representation
    '%x': r'.+',         # Locale's appropriate date representation
    '%X': r'.+',         # Locale's appropriate time representation
    '%%': r'%',          # Literal % character
}


def dt_format_to_regex(format):
    """Convert a C standard datetime format string to a regex pattern.

    Supports common strftime/%-format codes:
      %Y %y %m %d %H %I %M %S %f %z %Z %a %A %b %B %c %x %X %%

    The resulting pattern can be used directly with re.match() or compiled
    into a Parser for flexible datetime parsing.

    >>> dt_format_to_regex('%Y-%m-%d')
    '\\\\d{4}-\\\\d{1,2}-\\\\d{1,2}'
    >>> dt_format_to_regex('%H:%M:%S')
    '\\\\d{1,2}:\\\\d{1,2}:\\\\d{1,2}'
    """
    result = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(format):
        if format[i] == '%' and i + 1 < len(format):
            code = format[i:i+2]
            if code in _DT_FORMAT_CODES:
                result.append(_DT_FORMAT_CODES[code])
                i += 2
            else:
                # Unknown format code - escape it literally
                result.append(re.escape(code))
                i += 2
        else:
            result.append(re.escape(format[i]))
            i += 1
    return ''.join(result)
